root_cause.text: In the ets qdisc change handler, when a class transitions from DRR to strict priority, the code does not remove the class from the active list, causing a subsequent transition back to DRR to add it again, resulting in a list double-add corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "Whenever a user issues an ets qdisc change command, transforming a drr class into a strict one, the ets code isn't checking whether that class was in the active list and removing it. This means that, if a user changes a strict class (which was in the active list) back to a drr one, that class will be added twice to the active list." The patch adds a loop (for i = q->nstrict; i < nstrict; i++) that calls list_del_init(&q->classes[i].alist) for active classes transitioning to strict, fixing the missing removal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing cleanup of ETS active list when strict band count is increased.
intent_record.what: Added a loop that iterates from q->nstrict to nstrict-1, and for each class that is active, calls list_del_init on its alist.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when nstrict increases, classes that were previously in the ETS region (indices from old nstrict to new nstrict-1) are removed from the active list, preventing them from being scheduled with the ETS algorithm while they are now strict.

grouping_result.intent: Fix missing cleanup of ETS active list when strict band count is increased.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by fixing the missing cleanup of the ETS active list when a class transitions to strict priority, preventing a double-add corruption.

candidates.rationale: Updating nstrict without removing classes that transition from DRR to strict priority from the active list causes them to be re-added later when transitioning back to DRR, leading to active list double-add corruption.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement updates the number of strict priority bands without first removing classes that transition from DRR to strict priority from the active list. When a class later transitions back to DRR, the stale active list entry is still present, and the class is added again, causing a list double-add corruption.
